_note: Safe-first care cards shown BEFORE and alongside an online vet. The AI only CHOOSES a card and an urgency; it never writes medical advice, names a medicine or gives a dose. Status: drafted from the sources below; awaiting review by a partner veterinarian before launch.

urgency_words.emergency: Emergency: go to a vet or call 1962 now
urgency_words.this_week: See a vet in the next few days
urgency_words.watch: Watch at home and talk to a vet if it doesn't improve

maggot_wound.title: Wound with maggots (worms in a wound)
do_now: Keep flies away: cover the area loosely with a clean cloth if the animal allows it.
Keep the animal in shade and offer clean water.
Note where the wound is and how big it looks, for the vet.
dont: Don't pour kerosene, petrol, phenyl, acid or engine oil on the wound. They burn and poison the animal.
Don't try to pull maggots out deep inside the wound yourself.
maggot_wound.see_vet: Maggots eat living tissue and spread fast. A vet should clean and treat it today.

vomiting_diarrhoea.title: Vomiting or loose motions
do_now: Keep clean drinking water available in small amounts.
Keep a puppy or kitten warm and away from other dogs.
Note how many times, and whether there is blood.
dont: Don't give human medicines.
Don't force food.
vomiting_diarrhoea.see_vet: In puppies, vomiting with bloody motions can be parvovirus, which is deadly and spreads to other dogs. See a vet today; sooner if there is blood, weakness or the animal stops drinking.

not_eating.title: Not eating or very weak
do_now: Offer clean water and a little of the animal's usual food.
Check for ticks, wounds or a swollen belly.
Note since when it stopped eating.
dont: Don't force-feed.
Don't give human medicines or tonics.
not_eating.see_vet: Not eating for more than a day, or with fever, weakness or pale gums, needs a vet soon.

skin_itching.title: Itching, hair loss or skin sores (mange)
do_now: Keep the animal's bedding clean.
Wash your hands after touching it; some mange spreads to other animals and people.
Take a clear photo of the skin for the vet.
dont: Don't apply engine oil, kerosene or harsh chemicals.
Don't shave or scrub wounds.
skin_itching.see_vet: Mange is treatable, but the right medicine depends on the type. A vet should see it in the next few days.

ticks_fever.title: Ticks, fever or pale gums
do_now: Keep the animal in shade with water.
Check the gums: pale or yellow gums are a warning sign.
Note if it is weak or not eating.
dont: Don't apply pesticides or chemicals meant for crops.
Don't crush ticks with bare hands.
ticks_fever.see_vet: Tick fever can destroy red blood cells. Weakness, fever or pale gums need a vet today.

wound_bleeding.title: Wound or bleeding
do_now: Keep yourself safe: a hurt animal can bite or kick.
If it is calm and you are trained, press a clean cloth on a bleeding wound.
Keep it calm and still.
dont: Don't put turmeric, oil, powders or chemicals on the wound.
wound_bleeding.see_vet: Deep wounds and bleeding that doesn't stop need a vet today.

limping.title: Limping or can't stand
do_now: Keep the animal still and in shade.
If it was hit by a vehicle, report it as an SOS so a rescuer comes.
dont: Don't try to straighten or splint the leg.
Don't make it walk.
limping.see_vet: An animal that can't stand or put weight on a leg may have a fracture. A vet should examine it today.

eye_problem.title: Eye injury or discharge
do_now: Keep the animal out of dust and bright sun.
Take a clear photo of the eye for the vet.
dont: Don't put human eye drops, oil or kajal in the eye.
eye_problem.see_vet: A swollen, cloudy or injured eye should be seen soon; the same day if it was hit.

breathing_seizure.title: Trouble breathing, fits or collapse
do_now: Keep people back and the area quiet.
Move sharp objects away during a fit; don't hold the animal down.
Get to a vet now or call 1962.
dont: Don't put your hand in the animal's mouth.
Don't give water or food during a fit.

poisoning.title: Ate poison or something harmful
do_now: Keep the packet or a photo of what it ate.
Go to a vet now or call 1962.
dont: Don't make the animal vomit unless a vet tells you to.
Don't give milk, oil or home remedies.

lumpy_skin.title: Lumps on the skin of a cow or buffalo
do_now: Keep the animal apart from other cattle.
Control flies and mosquitoes around it.
Inform a vet or call 1962: it may be lumpy skin disease.
dont: Don't share water troughs or feed with other cattle.
Don't apply chemicals to the lumps.
lumpy_skin.see_vet: Lumpy skin disease spreads through insects. A vet should confirm it; vaccination protects other cattle nearby.

bloat.title: Swollen left belly in a cow (bloat)
do_now: Keep the animal standing and walking slowly if it can.
Call a vet or 1962 now.
dont: Don't let it keep eating.
Don't pierce the belly yourself.
bloat.see_vet: Bloat can kill within hours. This is an emergency.

plastic_eating.title: Cow eating plastic or garbage
do_now: Note if it is eating less, losing weight or not chewing the cud.
Keep plastic and garbage away from where it feeds.
dont: Don't feed it food wrapped in plastic bags.
plastic_eating.see_vet: Plastic builds up in the stomach over months. A vet can check a cow that is eating less or losing weight.

bite_rabies_risk.title: Animal that bit someone, or acting strangely
do_now: Keep a safe distance; don't try to catch it.
Anyone bitten or scratched: wash the wound with soap and running water for 15 minutes and get a rabies vaccine today.
dont: Don't touch its saliva.
Don't harm the animal; inform the municipal animal team or a vet.
bite_rabies_risk.see_vet: Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms start, and fully preventable with prompt vaccination.

general.title: General care while you wait for the vet
do_now: Keep the animal in shade with clean water.
Take clear photos and note when it started.
dont: Don't give human medicines.
Don't apply home remedies to wounds.
general.see_vet: A vet can tell you what this is. If it gets worse, call 1962.
